messages:
maya: quick sync — new 4-bit PTQ reranker (v4-4bit) shows ~1.8% NDCG@10 regression vs fp16 on our cross-domain bench. Not huge but consistent.
dan: is it across the board or concentrated?
maya: concentrated on long-doc slices (doc_tokens > 1200) and when the relevant passage is near chunk/truncation boundaries.
hao: do we still evaluate with passage-chunking? I recall eval harness chunks into 256-token passages and scores top-k per doc. Prod does concat + truncate to 512. That mismatch could flip which passage is scored.
sara: that'll definitely change ranking distribution. Does quant make it worse?
maya: 8-bit earlier was close (~0.2% delta). 4-bit delta is bigger and seems amplified when the gold passage is close to the truncated edge.
dan: can you run the three arms: fp16 concat-trunc, 4bit concat-trunc, and 4bit chunked (current eval)? Produce top1 swap CSV so we can attribute flips to chunking vs quantization.
maya: running now. commands: \n```
# concat-trunc eval (simulate prod)
python eval_harness.py --strategy=concat_trunc --max_total=512 --model=rerank-v4-fp16 --out=fp16_concat.csv
# 4-bit concat-trunc
python eval_harness.py --strategy=concat_trunc --max_total=512 --model=rerank-v4-4bit --out=4bit_concat.csv
# 4-bit chunked (baseline eval)
python eval_harness.py --strategy=chunked_passages --passage_len=256 --topk_per_doc=3 --model=rerank-v4-4bit --out=4bit_chunked.csv
```\nops-bot: job started: rerank-2145678901 (run=9912).\nhao: include columns: query_id, gold_pos_pct, baseline_rank, ptq_rank, swap_type (chunking_only|quant_amplified|other). Also capture tokenized offsets.
maya: will. saving flips to s3://rerank-artifacts/2145678901/flips.csv. ETA ~18m.
sara: after that we should compute: 1) fraction of queries where chunking alone changes top1 (compare fp16_concat vs fp16_chunked), 2) fraction where quant amplifies (compare 4bit_concat vs fp16_concat), 3) intersection.
dan: agree. Also compute per-slice deltas by gold_pos_pct (0-10%, 10-30%, 30-70%, 70-100%).
hao: if chunking explains most flips, fix eval to simulate prod concat_trunc for onboarding checks. If quant-specific, we need augmentation or retraining.
maya: preliminary numbers from partial run (5k queries): chunking-only flips ~0.9% of queries, quant-amplified flips ~0.7%, overlap ~0.2%. So both matter.
sara: thanks — that shows changing eval helps detect chunking issues but quant still introduces additional failures.
dan: mitigation plan: short term, update onboarding checklist to require concat-trunc passing on a prod-like sample. medium term, add truncation-jitter augmentation (+/-64 tokens) to the eval harness and reranker fine-tuning.
hao: also consider a small runtime shim that pads anchors up to 512 before tokenization when available on Dedicated deployments — less feasible on Hosted unless we quantify cost delta.
maya: cost estimate for padding everywhere: ~+5-7% tokens/request on long-context traffic. I'll run a Dedicated canary to measure real cost & latency.
ops-bot: job completed: rerank-2145678901 (run=9912) status=success. artifacts: s3://rerank-artifacts/2145678901/{flips.csv,summary.json}.
maya: uploaded summary with per-slice NDCG/MRR and example flip pairs (tokenized offsets). link above. tagging @hao @sara for analysis.
hao: I'll run causal attribution scripts to label flips as chunking_delta vs quant_delta and post a short note with recommendations.
sara: once we agree, can someone open PR to: 1) add concat_trunc gate in model onboarding, 2) add truncation-jitter augmentation in eval harness, 3) add small doc with pros/cons of changing prod truncation vs eval?
dan: I'll own the PR for onboarding checklist. maya — can you draft the augmentation code snippet?
maya: sure — I'll attach a minimal patch and sample metrics in the PR. ETA end of day.
dan: great, thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
